messages.subject: [statnet_help] structure - attribute interactions
messages.body_plain:
If your network has a vertex attribute named (say) "Sex" that gives  
the sex of each individual, you should be able to use

gwdegree(0.5, TRUE, "Sex")

This is not documented, but in a quick test it seems to work okay for  
me:

 > data(faux.mesa.high)
 > summary(faux.mesa.high~gwdegree(0.5, fixed=TRUE))
gwdegree
199.5657
 > summary(faux.mesa.high~gwdegree(0.5, TRUE, "Sex"))
gwdeg0.5.SexF gwdeg0.5.SexM
      105.5248       94.0409




Dave

messages.body_plain:
George Barnett just published a paper on this in the latest issue of Connections and I think he referenced software. Many software packages handle weighted links. The particulars depend on the package. For a weighted version of betweenness, look at Information Centrality in W&F.

I know ORA has weighted degree and Info Centrality. I imagine George's new measure will be in an upcoming version.

Ian

Ian,

Thanks for the help.  I have done extensive analysis of weighted edge
networks in UCI*NET.  I was hoping that statnet would accomodate this
as well; it would be nice to be able to script all of my analysis in
one tool, and I am actually pretty close.  Having used UCI*NET for so
long, it did not occur to me that one would do network analysis
without weighted edges.

Are there R packages other than iGraph that support analysis of weight
networks?  (Sorry, I don't know what ORA refers to).

I have relied on the Carter Butts and Hancock papers from the journal
of statistical software for my R SNA retooling.  I was hoping that
weighted edges were a statnet feature simply not covered in the
articles.

If ORA is an R package, I could be set!  I have found iGraph to be
powerful for visualizing weighted networks (far more flexible than
Netdraw.).  I can't say enough about how impressed I am with the tools
in R!

Thanks!!

Sean

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Re: package SNA with a weighted network - gplot / does SNA address weighted networks?

messages.body_plain:
Hi Sean.  I'm actually sitting next to Carter right now and he assures  
me that gplot can do this.

I believe that the problem is that you can't pass edge.len as a name  
of an edge covariate; instead, you'd need to pull this edge covariate  
out of the network explicitly, then pass this matrix to gplot,  
something like this:

edgelen <- stRead %e% "weight"
plot(stRead, uselen=TRUE, edge.len = edgelen, usecurve=TRUE)

I'm not sure whether this syntax will work for your example because I  
can't test it (I don't have your network object), but I believe it  
should.   HTH,

Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGM - too many unique dyads
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am running into what I think is a memory-related error that I hope someone can help solve.  I am trying to estimate an ERGM on a network with 2,350 nodes.  On my PC I have tried increasing the memory using 'memory.limit(3000)'  I have also tried running in 64-bit R on a mac.  Both produce the same error.  I'm using version 2.2-4 of statnet.

Here is the error message:

Error in ergm.pl(Clist = Clist, Clist.miss = Clist.miss, m = m, theta.offset = theta.offset,  :
  Too many unique dyads!

Here is the model I am trying to estimate.

> model1<- ergm (recnet~ edges + nodematch("educ") + nodematch("sex") + nodematch("race") + nodematch("grade") + absdiff("gpa") + absdiff("probbhvr") + absdiff("health") + absdiff("depres") +
gwdegree(.25, fixed=TRUE) + gwdsp(.25, fixed=TRUE) + gwesp(.25, fixed=TRUE))

I know I could do some recoding to simplify the measurement of variables (i.e., converting numeric scales to integers).  But, I would prefer to keep measures in their original metrics if possible.

Any insight would be appreciated.
--David

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGM - too many unique dyads
messages.body_plain:
Hi David.  You are correct that this is a memory-related error.   
You're getting the error because (a) your network has more than 1  
million possible edges; and (b) the model you're using uses quantative  
variables in such a way that most vectors of "change statistics" (each  
possible edge gets its own such vector) are completely unique, which  
means that you're not able to take advantage of ergm's default  
compression algorithm, which basically stores only the unique change  
statistic vectors (and keeps a count of the number of times each one  
is used).  All of this information is fed into the logistic regression  
solver that returns the MPLE for you.

In any case, the error you're seeing should be pretty easy to fix,  
though the error message you got should be more informative about how  
to fix it!  (I'll make a change for the next version of ergm).  The  
key is changing the default value (which is 1 million) of the control  
parameter called "maxNumDyadTypes" using the control.ergm function.

I'll use the faux.magnolia.high dataset to demonstrate, since it has  
1461 nodes and 1461-choose-2 is just big enough to go over a million.   
First, here's what happens before changing the default:

 > data(faux.magnolia.high)
 > fmh <- faux.magnolia.high
 > fmh %v% "quantitative.var" <- rnorm(1461)
 > ergm(fmh ~ absdiff("quantitative.var"))
Error in ergm.pl(Clist = Clist, Clist.miss = Clist.miss, m = m,  
theta.offset = theta.offset,  :
   Too many unique dyads!

Now for the control.ergm function:

 > big.enough <- 1461 * 1460 / 2
 > ergm(fmh ~ absdiff("quantitative.var"),  
control=control.ergm(maxNumDyadTypes=big.enough))
Newton-Raphson iterations:  12

MLE Coefficients:
absdiff.quantitative.var
                   -20.49

Hope this helps.

Dave

messages.body_plain:
Hello Ick Hoon,

I'm sorry it took so long to deal with this one.  This was a bug that  
I inadvertently introduced when I modified the simulating  
functionality of ergm.  I believe I have now fixed it; in any case, I  
now can run an example like yours without getting the same error.

I would like to upload a new version of ergm to CRAN with this fix  
(along with quite a few others that we've made recently), but now is  
not a good time to mess with the CRAN version because there is a  
workshop on statnet happening at the Sunbelt networks conference this  
week and uploading during this week could cause problems there.   As  
an alternative, I will post the source code of the new (beta) version  
of ergm_2.2-5 on my website at

http://www.stat.psu.edu/~dhunter/code/

If you find any additional problems, please let us know!  The new  
version should be on CRAN sometime next week.

Dave
